note: Full curriculum (Stage A -> B -> C) trained 2026-09-19 to 2026-09-21 on an RTX 4050 Laptop GPU. real_results below are measured, not targets. Stage A was undertrained (2/10 epochs, see reports/system_report.md SS1) but did not block Stage B/C from completing properly. 'rule_based_keyword_cue' and 'sentinel_vision_gate_rl' below are NOT verified -- see their own 'warning' fields -- and no script in this repo currently computes 'random' or 'single_frame_k1' under those exact names either; treat all four baselines/gate-result as unverified pending a real run via src/eval/run_benchmark.py with an actual checkpoints/gate_rl.pt.

rule_based_keyword_cue.warning: NOT an independent baseline. HARMFUL_CUES (src/data/loaders.py) is the SAME keyword rule used to weak-label the real-data training/eval splits (scripts/preprocess_real_data.py), so scoring this rule against those labels is tautological by construction -- the perfect 1.0/1.0/0.0 below is expected from that tautology, not evidence of a working rule-based detector. No script in this repo currently computes this exact baseline; these numbers were not produced by a run of src/eval/run_benchmark.py (whose only 'rule_based' baseline is an unrelated oracle placeholder, not a keyword matcher).

sentinel_vision_gate_rl.warning: UNVERIFIED. checkpoints/gate_rl.pt does not exist on disk in this repo, and src/eval/run_benchmark.py (the only script that evaluates a PPO gate) writes its result under the key 'sentinel_vision_gate', not 'sentinel_vision_gate_rl' -- and would silently skip gate evaluation entirely (no key written) if gate_rl.pt is missing, which it is. These numbers cannot have been produced by running the current code against a checkpoint that currently exists. Treat as unverified, same as the rule_based_keyword_cue baseline above, until a real gate_rl.pt is trained and this is re-run.

alternate_checkpoint_epoch_12.note: checkpoints/stage_c/epoch_15_final.pt (filename says 15, real weights are epoch 12 -- see trainer.py early-stopping checkpoint-naming fix). Better validation localization IoU (0.115) but WORSE held-out test precision/F1 than best.pt -- not recommended for deployment.

real_results.honest_assessment: Harmful-action recall improved substantially through the curriculum (0.46 -> 0.67 -> 0.74 on validation) and reaches 1.00 on the clean synthetic held-out test set, confirming the architecture and injection pipeline work. Bounding-box localization is weak across all checkpoints (IoU 0.03-0.12, well under the >0.65 target) -- the model detects risk far more reliably than it localizes it. Not yet at the >0.90 recall / >0.85 precision targets on the harder validation mix.
real_results.unresolved_discrepancy: This block's validation_set.risk_precision (0.6074) does not match baselines.sentinel_vision_no_gate.precision (0.5251) above, despite both citing the same recall (0.7435) for nominally the same checkpoint/split. Also, n_samples here (2,785) does not match the N=3,167 figure previously stated in paper/benchmark_tables/table1_main_benchmark.tex's caption for the same evaluation. Neither has been reconciled by re-running the eval; flagged rather than silently repeated.
